ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders and UBOs against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions regimes, OFAC SDN list where USD transactions are anticipated, and Spain's domestic terrorism financing lists. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must undergo enhanced due diligence under Article 11 of Ley 10/2010; evidence of source of funds and wealth required for PEP-linked investments. Suspicious transactions must be reported to SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales y Obligaciones Privadas) through the prescribed ROS channel. Records must be preserved for 10 years after the business relationship is terminated.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) online name certification service via registradores.org
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The chosen corporate name may be expressed in Spanish or in any of Spain's co-official languages (Catalan, Basque, Galician or Valencian); it must use Latin script and must include Spanish accents correctly. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters. The legal form suffix must be 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the accepted abbreviation 'S.L.' (or 'S.R.L.'). The name must be factually accurate and must not mislead as to geographic or public character.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: For any term that suggests official sponsorship, public administration or regulated financial activity, prior ministerial or supervisory authorisation is required.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Mercantil Central declines the requested name, the applicant may file an administrative appeal ('recurso de alzada') before the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN) within one month of notification. The appeal must state the grounds for distinctiveness, provide available prior-name conflict evidence, and request reconsideration of the phonetic or graphical comparison. Where the rejection results from a similar existing name, the applicant may either submit a written consent, where legally permissible, or select a new alternative name and re-apply. A successful name reservation is valid for 90 days; if not used, it may be extended by re-applying to the RMC before expiration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a low-risk cloud infrastructure developer subject to compliance: the registered office must be a real physical address within Spain capable of receiving official notifications, service of proceedings, and tax authority correspondence. A virtual office is acceptable if it provides permanent reception, forwarding, and a dedicated Spanish tax address; full physical substance is not required for this business model, but the company must maintain adequate books, customer records, and administrative oversight from Spain.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 10%) for a newly incorporated SL in the ISIC 6201 low-risk cloud tools sector; the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) may conduct occasional on-site verification when VAT refunds, non-resident ownership or material cross-border operations trigger audit thresholds.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), arts. 20-23, 28, 58 and 62; Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil), arts. 173-175; Ley 14/2013 on the sociedades limitadas de formación sucesiva (SLFS) regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name clearance); Notary Public (execution of deed); Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office (inscription); Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (NIF issuance).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public deed of incorporation) filed for registration in the Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital required for the SL under this pipeline profile; capital may be fixed at a nominal amount and must be fully subscribed and paid-in at subscription, in cash or in kind. No escrow account is required. If capital is set below the historical €3,000 threshold, the SLFS reserve and distribution restrictions apply until capital plus reserves reach €3,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The deed of incorporation and the statutes of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada are approved and ratified. (2) The shares subscribed by the founding members are allotted fully paid as set forth in the incorporation deed. (3) The registered office is fixed at [registered-office address], Madrid, Spain. (4) [Administrator Name] is appointed sole administrator, with all powers granted under the statutes, including opening bank accounts, executing agreements, and engaging employees. (5) The administrator is authorized to obtain the provisional NIF, register the company in the Registro Mercantil, publish the incorporation notice, and make all tax, social security, and municipal filings. (6) All acts performed by the administrator in connection with the incorporation prior to this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance at the Central Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a single online application with up to three proposed corporate names ending in 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'SL'; attach founders' identification and proof of fee payment; receive the Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social confirming name availability.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all founding members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or the certificate is suspended, file a revised application with alternate names within the statutory period; if unjustly refused, appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial execution of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public selected by the founding members
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the name certificate and draft articles of association (estatutos) to the notary; founding members execute the public deed of incorporation, acknowledging full subscription and payment of share capital, shareholder identity, corporate purpose, registered-office address, and first administrator appointments.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE of all shareholders
Bank certificate or other proof of capital contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a deficiency note or refuses execution, correct the articles or supporting documentation, reconvene the shareholders, and resubmit for a new deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provisional NIF application and opening of corporate bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed deed to AEAT using Modelo 036 to obtain the provisional NIF; open a corporate bank account in the name of the SL and deposit the subscribed capital; obtain a bank certificate confirming the contribution for later registry inscription.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized incorporation deed
Power of attorney of the legal representative
Identification documents of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT queries the application, supply the requested deed translations or supplementary documentation; if the bank delays, escalate to the corporate desk or select another authorized credit entity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized deed and ancillary documents for registration with the Provincial Commercial Registry; pay the official registry fee; obtain the certificate of inscription (certificación de inscripción) that confers legal personality.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a suspension or defect note, amend the deed or supply missing evidence within the cure period and refile; appeal adverse decisions before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social; municipal licensing authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the registry inscription certificate with AEAT to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF; file the municipal start-of-activity declaration (IAE); register with Social Security if hiring staff; obtain the municipal prior-activity communication or operating license for the physical office premises.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation from the Registro Mercantil
Lease agreement or title over the registered office
Municipal activity license forms or technical declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax, social security, or municipal filings are queried, submit additional technical reports, plans, or corrections; appeal adverse municipal decisions through the competent administrative review procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid - Municipal Department of Economic Activities and Licenses (Municipal activity licensing authority for the registered office)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Comunicación Previa de Actividad Económica / Licencia de Apertura (prior communication of economic activity or opening license)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) and the competent Consejería de Medio Ambiente of the Autonomous Community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - non-industrial office and cloud-infrastructure activity under ISIC 6201; no full EIA or integrated environmental authorization required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No significant wastewater or VOC emissions expected; compliance with municipal wastewater discharge bylaws, Real Decreto 102/2011 on air quality, noise/vibration limits, and WEEE recycling obligations for electronic equipment is recommended and verified at municipal inspection.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate for office premises under CTE DB-SI, structural load inspection for server/storage areas, and occupational workplace clearance under Ley 31/1995 and Real Decreto 486/1997, including the preemptive risk assessment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Sede Electrónica — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of the SL, the notary files the deed through the Single Electronic Window (CIRCE/DUE) and the system issues a provisional corporate NIF. Within two months of the deed, the administrator must submit Form 030/036 to the competent AEAT office (or electronically with a digital certificate) to obtain the definitive NIF (one letter identifying the legal form followed by 8 digits, e.g., B-12345678 for an SL), and to register the company in the Census of Entrepreneurs. Non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment require a separate non-resident NIF (Form 036, 'N' prefix) when holding Spanish assets or executing taxable transactions; the SL itself is the relevant taxable person for Spanish income tax and VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Spain. The SL is mandatorily a separate taxable person under Ley 27/2014 (LIS). Statutory elections available: (i) consolidated tax group regime (Art. 64 LIS) for groups with ≥75% control; (ii) VAT cash-accounting criteria de caja (Art. 163 decies LIVA) for SMEs with turnover ≤ €2M; (iii) monthly VAT return/refund regime (REDEME, Art. 35 RD 1624/1992) for monthly refund recovery; (iv) One-Stop-Shop (OSS) registration for intra-community distance sales and cross-border B2C digital services; (v) patent-box reduction (Art. 23 LIS) for in-house developed IP. Hybrid-mismatch rules under ATAD (Law 11/2021) apply automatically without elective opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido — IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 0.00 EUR — no de minimis turnover threshold; VAT registration is compulsory upon commencement of any taxable economic activity. An EUR 10,000 OSS threshold applies only to intra-community distance sales to non-taxable persons and is not applicable to B2B DevTools cloud service supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información): mandatory near-real-time filing of issuance and received VAT records via AEAT web-service APIs (X.509 authentication) within 4 calendar days (8 in July) for large enterprises (turnover > €6M) and REDEME opt-ins. Verifactu (RD 1007/2023): all billing software must be certified, generating QR-stamped, algorithmically verifiable invoices; B2B electronic invoicing under Ley Crea y Crece is phased in from 2025–2026 for enterprises with turnover > €8M. No transactional preprint/digital-stamping clearance is required at standard invoice level.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: DevTools/API-monitoring SaaS qualifies for export zero-rating: (i) intra-EU B2B supplies — place of supply is the customer's country (Art. 70 LIVA), invoice must show the customer's valid EU VAT ID and 'inversión del sujeto pasivo' (reverse charge), so no Spanish VAT; (ii) non-EU B2B supplies — Art. 69.1 LIVA places the supply outside Spanish territory, no Spanish VAT applies; (iii) exported physical hardware/appliances qualify for the Art. 21.1 LIVA export exemption with credit (0%) upon customs evidence. Supplies to Spanish-established customers are subject to 21% VAT; the 0% carve-out applies only to customers established abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA / Export declaration summary record) — required only for physical goods exports; not applicable to pure SaaS/cloud services
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR transport document — required only for physical goods exports; not applicable to digital delivery
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT payment receipt from the foreign client — AEAT evidentiary practice for zero-rated services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline, but AEAT audit practice treats export payments outstanding beyond 180 days from invoice as presumptive evidence of a domestic taxable supply, triggering reassessment with late interest (Art. 26 LGT) and an infringement surcharge of 50%–150% of the VAT under Art. 191 LGT. Falsified export documentation or abusive zero-rating claims can amount to criminal tax fraud under Art. 305 Código Penal where defrauded tax exceeds EUR 120,000 per period, with penalties of imprisonment and full clawback. The complete evidence package (contract, service-rendering logs, VIES validation, client tax-residence certificate, and payment receipts) must be retained for the four-year statute of limitation (Art. 66 LGT).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) — the national central bank and the authority responsible for balance-of-payments statistics and foreign-exchange oversight within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB). FX control powers are exercised within the Eurosystem framework, while the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (Foreign Investment Register), operated by the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio under the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise, administers FDI filings. SEPBLAC, Spain's Financial Intelligence Unit, completes the regulatory perimeter for AML/CTF screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted euro convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions pursuant to Article 63 TFEU and the EU Capital Movements Directive. Spain imposes no general exchange-control authorization for trade, services, or financial flows. The only legal hurdles to profit remittance are documentary: (i) the distributing SL must hold sufficient distributable reserves per audited financial statements; (ii) dividends to non-resident shareholders are subject to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR, withholding generally 19%, reduced or eliminated by an applicable Double Tax Treaty or by the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where a qualifying EU/EEA parent holds at least 10%); and (iii) statistical and FDI filings must be current. An ISIC 6201 dev-tools cloud business is categorized as Low_Risk_Standard for AML purposes, which materially de-risks convertibility, onboarding, and remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no repatriation timeline, and no forced conversion ratio. The Spanish SL may hold export receipts freely in EUR or foreign currency. Cross-border transaction reporting to the Banco de España for balance-of-payments statistics remains obligatory for operations exceeding the threshold set by applicable Bank of Spain circulars, customarily EUR 50,000 per commercial-services operation; non-compliance produces administrative penalties only and does not invalidate the underlying receipt. The bank ordinarily submits the declaration automatically on the client's behalf.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Operational Current Account (EUR); Multi-Currency USD/GBP overlay for cloud-vendor payments
Capital Escrow / Equity Contribution Deposit Account (Notary Certificate) and Operational Account
Operational Account with Stripe settlement, SEPA Instant, and dedicated foreign-payment desk
Operational Account with cross-border FX desk and trade-finance line for LATAM distribution
Operational Account / Treasury deposit and designated USD collection account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH. EU-licensed EMIs (Wise, Qonto, Revolut Business, and Spanish EMIs such as Bnext) may open accounts fully remotely and provide SEPA and SEPA Instant IBANs, making them efficient collection and disbursement overlays for recurring subscription billing and small-vendor payments. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI is not a deposit-taking credit institution under Law 10/2010, so it cannot fully substitute for a Banco de España-supervised account for capital escrow, statutory equity compliance, or significant FDI filings; (ii) Mercury, a US-domiciled fintech rather than an EU EMI, is viable only as a USD collection and ACH rail, requiring a US EIN and US Corporate Transparency Act/BOI compliance, and its role must remain subordinate to the Spanish anchor account; (iii) lack of Spanish deposit-guarantee coverage and concentration risk argue against holding the full treasury on an EMI. Recommended structure: one Tier-1 Spanish anchor account, one EU EMI as an operational circuit, and one Mercury USD account as a collection overlay.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Law 10/2010 requires personal identification of the Administrador Único and all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs). Most Tier-1 banks require the director or a duly empowered representative to appear in person at a Spanish branch for initial onboarding; remote video KYC is accepted at Santander, BBVA, and CaixaBank for low-risk technology companies when the director holds an EU/EEA passport or a Spanish NIE and the registered office can be independently verified. When the director is non-resident and lacks an NIE, the bank mandates a notarized Power of Attorney (Poder General) legalized with a Hague Apostille, certified passport copies, a bank reference from the remitting institution, and physical identity verification of the appointed apoderado in Spain. A full face-to-face interview may be waived only where the UBO is resident in a low-risk jurisdiction, the corporate file is complete, and the expected transaction profile matches a Low_Risk_Standard software exporter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO resident in a jurisdiction classified by the European Commission or SEPBLAC as high-risk (including certain LATAM jurisdictions) or involvement of a shell/offshore holding chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport; NIE certificate or application receipt; Hague-apostilled notarized power of attorney addressed to the Spanish bank; clean criminal-record certificate (certificado de antecedentes penales) from the residency jurisdiction; signed PEP declaration; corporate sociograma descending to natural-person UBOs; Spain economic-substance bundle including registered-office lease, payroll records, social-security affiliations, hyperscaler agreements, and client contracts; written commercial explanation of any genuine nexus with the high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound equity injection that is disproportionately large relative to forecast revenue, headcount, and cash burn, triggering source-of-wealth concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Escritura de Ampliación de Capital registered in the Registro Mercantil; sworn statement of lawful source of funds; audited financial statements or personal tax returns of the shareholder covering the remitting account; bank-to-bank reference and account-activity summary from the remitting bank; 24-month treasury forecast; evidence of committed commercial contracts (Stripe MRR report, AWS/Azure/GCP agreements); appointment of a compliance officer under Law 10/2010; company AML risk manual reflecting the Low_Risk_Standard rating.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent outbound disbursements to non-OECD software contractors, data centers, or channel partners located in opaque jurisdictions that do not align with the documented SaaS supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements, order forms, and itemized supplier invoices; dated service-delivery evidence including SLAs, uptime metrics, tickets, and logs; PEP and sanctions screening reports for every counterparty; internal treasury approval memoranda; annual AML risk assessment confirming Low_Risk_Standard; segregation-of-duties matrix within finance; VAT-compliant documentation (reverse-charge treatment on B2B cross-border services).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipts from cryptocurrency exchanges or virtual-asset service providers (VASPs), use of pre-funded cards, or a shared/virtual-office registered address that fails the economic-substance screen.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts proving the underlying software subscription or service; source-of-funds certificates from regulated VASPs; board resolution confirming that the company does not accept crypto-asset payments; registered-office domiciliation agreement and a current utility bill in the corporate name; notarial certificate of the domicilio social; declaration of absence of undisclosed shareholders; Spanish tax filings (Modelo 200, Modelo 303, Modelo 190) evidencing alignment between invoiced revenue, banking flows, and declared taxable base.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity route: execute an 'escritura pública de ampliación de capital' before a Spanish notary, deposit the consideration into the designated Capital Escrow or corporate operational account, and transmit via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA CT with remittance information explicitly reading 'Suscripción y desembolso de participaciones sociales / aportación de capital a ES_SL NIF [company NIF]'. The remitting bank should apply the Banco de España balance-of-payments classification 'direct investment – equity capital' (inversión directa – capital), and the receiving bank must issue the deposit certificate required by the notary. Shareholder-loan route: execute a notarized loan agreement where the term exceeds one year or security is granted, remit under the concept 'préstamo accionista a ES_SL', apply arm's-length interest under Article 16 of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law and OECD TP Guidelines, and meet any Spanish source-withholding obligations on interest. Both routes require a post-closing filing with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores within one month (simplified statistical declaration for amounts below EUR 3,005,060.52; full declaration above that statutory threshold). Treasury must reconcile the SWIFT confirmation, the notarial deed, the capital-deposit certificate, and the FDI filing receipt before funds are released for operations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing architecture: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) for all EUR vendor and intra-EU settlements within the standard T+1 or SEPA Instant window, carrying a structured creditor reference to avoid reconciliation friction; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR payments (USD, GBP, LATAM currencies), including complete beneficiary details, invoice reference in field 70, and the Banco de España outward-payment statistical code for 'computer services / software subscriptions'; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600, irrevocable, at sight) for LATAM distributors or resellers requiring documentary trade security, with the Spanish Tier-1 bank as confirming/advising bank; (iv) US hyperscaler payments and AWS/Azure/GCP disbursements via SWIFT or via Merchant/Vendor ACH using the Mercury USD account, each matched to the invoice reference; (v) for all operations above the applicable Banco de España reporting threshold, the bank files the automatic IOE/balance-of-payments declaration, and treasury must retain the complete evidentiary file comprising invoices, contracts, delivery logs, and bank confirmations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Outright Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for hedging recurring USD subscription revenue and cloud-vendor costs
FX Vanilla European Options and Zero-Cost Collars covering USD income against EUR operating expenditures
FX Swaps (spot/forward combinations) for short-dated liquidity bridging between USD receipts and EUR disbursements
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible LATAM currency exposures (e.g., ARS, VES, COP) where physical deliverability is legally or practically unavailable
Cross-Currency Swaps (XCCY) for long-term intercompany financing and for lag mitigation on large equity subscription inflows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalisation of accounting books and corporate books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the financial year, normally by 30 April for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential registry rejection, evidentiary limitations, and administrative liability; late legalisation may impede subsequent filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial year, normally by 30 June for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure may result in director liability and delay or prevent statutory filing of the annual accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval, normally by 31 July for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Registry may close the company's registration after one year from the filing deadline. Fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, subject to applicable statutory limits and company size; higher limits may apply in larger cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration accompanying annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry and Central Register of Beneficial Ownership where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with each annual accounts deposit and updated promptly following any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry rejection, inability to complete the annual accounts deposit, and potential administrative sanctions for inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated beneficial ownership information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period; normally 1 to 25 July for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties generally apply under the General Tax Law; unpaid tax also incurs late-payment interest, collection surcharges, and possible tax inspection penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate tax prepayments, Modelo 202, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December, subject to the applicable calculation method and taxpayer status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or insufficient payment may trigger surcharges, late-payment interest, and penalties under Spanish tax procedure rules.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets above EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover above EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce above 50 employees. Additional mandatory-audit rules apply to certain regulated, public-interest, group, or subsidised entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish accounting legislation. IFRS is generally relevant for consolidated accounts of listed groups and other specifically regulated cases, not as the ordinary framework for a privately held Spanish SL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain current beneficial ownership information and record shareholding transfers in the Register of Members. Beneficial ownership information is confirmed through the beneficial ownership declaration filed with the annual accounts and must be updated after changes in ownership or control. There is generally no separate standalone annual UBO return for an ordinary SL apart from the applicable registry filings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Contracts with the Sole Shareholder, if the company has a sole shareholder
Accounting books and supporting corporate resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-1,650 annually for a basic registered-office and corporate secretarial package
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,500-5,000 for a small SL requiring a statutory audit; no statutory audit fee applies where the company is not subject to mandatory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general Spanish corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); 15% for qualifying newly incorporated SLs in the first two taxable periods with positive taxable base; 15% reduced rate for certified 'startups' under Law 28/2022 for up to four tax periods, subject to eligibility conditions including lack of prior group listing and annual turnover under EUR 5 million.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Spanish law uses no registered tax amnesties or special-purpose tax holidays. Available effective-rate mechanisms include: 50% exemption on certain intellectual property income (patent box); 10% tax allowance for corporate withholding on income and profits ('reserva de capitalización'); R&D and innovation tax credits; 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividend income; indefinite utilisation of tax loss carryforwards subject to offset quotas.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically via AEAT Sede Electrónica / Mutual/CoDIN service. Quarterly preliminary instalments are declared on Modelo 202; related-party transaction information returns are filed on Modelo 232. The fiscal period level is the accounting year, typically calendar year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with four preliminary corporate income tax payments per tax year if taxable amount and thresholds are satisfied (Modelo 202).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Modelo 200 must be filed within 25 calendar days following the expiration of six months after the fiscal year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the statutory window runs from 1 July through 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: NIF, exact legal name, registered address and founding office data; non-resident representative identifier if a lean structure uses a Spanish director.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident member relying on an SL should maintain a Spanish NIF and identifiable beneficial owner form 099; no local PE is admissible unless fixed place in Spain is shown.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period and consolidation indicator: start date and end date of the tax year; sections for APAs and correcting returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL fiscal year rather than parent year; if changing year-end to match US or LatAm parent, file a Modelo 200 with shortened period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of net turnover amount and principal economic activity code ISIC 6201 / CNAE 6201.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify ancillary subscriptions and API usage fees under the same CNAE, and do not separate recurring cloud infrastructure revenue into unrelated trade categories.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prevailing negative tax base offsets claimed from prior periods, including pending net operating loss amounts and the applicable limit formula.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For offsetting losses of the pre-merger or pre-transfer period, obtain formal economic-substance evidence and file yearly loss trace schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Positive tax base produced after corrections for permanent differences, integration of double taxation claims, and international tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report any tax base derived from IP royalty or cloud licensing income separately; maintain transfer pricing documentation since related-party transactions are presumed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable type and coefficient: 25% general, 15% startup/newco, special rates for public listed investment vehicles appropriate to an SL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certified startup status is ineffective if the commercial owner or directors are shell nominees resident outside Spain; AEAT scrutinises real economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total quota and deductions: full income tax due, foreign tax credits, treaty-covered withholding credits, patent box exemption, and capitalisation allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding tax on payments received from abroad must be converted on the date of accrual and claimed under ordre public of the DTA if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments, withholdings and instalments already paid; result to be payable on balance sheet or refundable amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not include their own tax ID in this box; any Spanish WHT on a bank remittance is handled on the payer's Modelo 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior summons: surcharge under LGT Art. 27 at 5% per month for the first 12 months and 20% after 12 months; default interest accrues daily. Omission of relevant tax facts or under-declaration may generate a 50%-75% proportional penalty, and the taxpayer may be excluded from public credit relationships for criminal evasion over EUR 120,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% standard Spanish withholding tax for non-resident shareholders (Impuesto sobre la Renta de No Residentes, IRNR), unless a more favourable double taxation agreement or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption applies. Treaty rates commonly reduce Spanish dividend withholding to 5% for qualifying shareholdings of 10% or 7.5% for portfolio holdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA, the Spanish payer must receive a residence certificate issued by the tax authority of the recipient country, containing the NIF or functional equivalent, in the acceptable form and period requested by AEAT. For refunds, the non-resident files Form 210 (and dispositive statement of Form 211 when applicable) through the AEAT non-resident office; refund remedies must be brought within the four-year statute of limitations; the application must include the original Spanish withholding certificate and formal appointment of a representative if the non-resident has no registered office. EU directive relief requires a model 210 declaration, status as an EU/EEA company, 5% shareholding and a one-year or signed holding-period undertaking.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by an SL to non-residents are subject to 19% IRNR withholding under Spanish domestic law, reduced under most DTAs to 5%-10% for beneficial owners. Debt interest paid by an SL to non-resident creditors is generally subject to 19% domestic withholding, with DTA reductions commonly to 10% (15% for portfolio debt securities as negotiated; EU Directive rates may apply for certain permanent-interest debt instruments).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Spanish SL must prepare a Local File of related-party transactions where the value of transactions with any related person exceeds EUR 250,000 or regardless of amount when the net turnover exceeds EUR 45 million. A Master File is mandatory for groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EUR 75 million. Form 232 annual related-party disclosure is due where the volume of linked-party transactions exceeds EUR 250,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies EU ATAD limitations and the Spanish General Anti-Abuse Clause rather than a separate 'ESR' licence. For an SL, economic substance requires that key management and developer decisions, physical premises, risk-taking employees and a demonstrable payroll operate in Spain. Absence of substance abroad can result in CFC inclusion, deemed non-resident PE for permanent employees in LatAm or US jurisdictions, and denial of treaty benefits where a conduit registry fails the principal-purpose test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Concealed Subscription Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing developer-tool subscriptions, API usage fees or cloud infrastructure hosting revenue into offshore bank accounts, using factoring or merchant aggregator accounts in a third country without a meaningful sales presence, and omitting the resulting taxable base from Modelo 200.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may re-characterise revenue with a proportional penalty of 50%-100% of the concealed tax base plus late-payment interest. If the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000, Criminal Code Art. 305 applies with prison penalties of two to six years and a fine of six to twelve times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly omit income are jointly and severally liable under LGT Art. 42.2; civil restitution to the tax debt may cover principal, surcharge and interest. Criminal proceedings can impose travel bans, surrender of passport, provisional seizure of personal assets and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming an SL with no Spanish premises, no resident staff, no board meetings in Spain and no operational logistics, while re-invoicing development-tool licences or services to LatAm subsidiaries solely to absorb foreign revenue and obtain Spanish treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: General anti-abuse clause disapplies the legal form; related-party transactions are valued under the arm's-length standard; omitted income and imputed payments give rise to a revised tax debt with a 50% to 100% penalty. In hard-core conduit structures AEAT may impose permanent establishment income attribution on the offshore vendor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A Spanish court may pierce the corporate veil to reach the Spanish director's personal assets for unpaid tax debts; directors face administrative penalties under the Spanish AML Law for non-transparent beneficial ownership and possible a settlement order in tax fraud proceedings involving shell routing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing payments from high-risk clients, accepting cryptocurrency settlement without KYC/UBO verification, using merchant accounts in Panama or Singapore for Latin American customer invoices, or failing to file SARs and register the appointed compliance representative under Spanish Law 10/2010.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Very serious AML violations under Law 10/2010 carry fines up to EUR 1,500,000 (or 10% of the total balance sheet amount) and the mandatory proposal to ESMA/CNMV to revoke the company's payment-institution licence. Criminal conviction under Criminal Code Arts. 301-302 can impose imprisonment of one to four years plus fines of three to five times the disappeared amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable if they give consent, tolerate or fail to remedy laundering activity; civil conduct includes restitution to Spanish and foreign funds, personal financial sanctions, prohibitions on managing other companies and travel restrictions while subject to an ongoing criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Hidden Permanent Establishment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying artificial royalties or disguised interest to related vendors located in no-tax or low-tax jurisdictions for SaaS backend or toll-api services without comparable personnel costs; alternatively maintaining sales engineers and servers in a Latin American country in a manner that creates a PE under the Germany-Spain, US-Spain or LatAm DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may adjust the taxable base under the official comparability standard and impose a 10% surcharge on the adjustment, in addition to default interest. Failure to present the required TP documentation triggers fixed penalties of EUR 3,000 to EUR 10,500 per data item. If the adjustment exceeds EUR 25,000, a penalty of 50% applies in the presence of concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for undisclosed PE activity when the Spanish SL assumes commercial risks of a foreign office through an undocumented server or teleworking arrangement; the company's corporate veil is pierced in respect of unauthorised sub-agent liabilities, and directors may face personal recovery, travel bans if criminal charges are filed and imprisonment in aggravated VAT/tax fraud.
